name: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Stomach
aliases: Primary Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Stomach

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Gastric Squamous Cell Carcinoma

criteria.description: Presence of malignant squamous cells with keratinization and intercellular bridges on gastric biopsy
Exclusion of squamous cell carcinoma from other primary sites such as esophagus or skin
Positive immunohistochemical staining for squamous markers (e.g., p63, CK5/6) and negative for adenocarcinoma markers
Imaging evidence of a primary gastric mass without continuity with esophageal squamous carcinoma

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of squamous cell carcinoma in the stomach with exclusion of other primary sites and supportive immunohistochemistry
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires careful exclusion of metastatic or contiguous squamous cell carcinoma from adjacent organs.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Progressive dysphagia due to gastric outlet obstruction
searchTerms: worsening swallowing problems from stomach blockage
difficulty eating due to gastric outlet obstruction

pathognomonic.symptomName: Hematemesis with squamous cell carcinoma histology

searchTerms: severe weight loss with muscle loss

laboratory: Microcytic hypochromic anemia due to chronic blood loss
Elevated serum calcium in paraneoplastic syndrome
Elevated tumor markers such as SCC antigen
imaging: CT scan showing gastric wall thickening and mass lesion
Endoscopic ultrasound revealing hypoechoic gastric mass
PET-CT demonstrating localized metabolic activity without distant metastases
genetic: No specific germline mutations identified; somatic mutations may include TP53 alterations
other: Histopathology demonstrating keratin pearls and intercellular bridges
Immunohistochemistry positive for p63 and CK5/6

distinguishingFeatures: More common than squamous cell carcinoma
Tumor continuity with esophageal squamous carcinoma
History of esophageal cancer or dysplasia
Imaging showing extension from esophagus to stomach

redFlags: Rapid progression of dysphagia and weight loss
Evidence of gastrointestinal bleeding (hematemesis or melena)
Palpable abdominal mass with constitutional symptoms
references: Saito H, et al. Primary squamous cell carcinoma of the stomach: a case report and review of the literature. World J Gastroenterol. 2015.
Orphanet: Squamous cell carcinoma of the stomach (ORPHA:418959)
National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) Guidelines for Gastric Cancer, 2024
